root_cause: Splenic rupture from infectious mononucleosis (mono) after a tackle

patient.name: Jonah Reyes
patient.background: University rugby player, recent 'bad flu' with sore throat, otherwise healthy

findings.result: Atypical lymphocytes, positive mono spot test (EBV)
Mildly raised liver enzymes (hepatitis), liver mildly enlarged
Fast heart rate, low pressure (hypovolemic shock)
Left shoulder joint and collarbone normal, no fracture
No head bleed; fainting from low blood flow (syncope)
Mild irritation from ibuprofen (gastritis), no perforation
Left kidney intact, small urine output (oliguria)

treatments.name: Fluids, blood, emergency splenectomy
treatments.why: Replacing lost blood and removing or repairing the torn spleen stops the bleeding at its source.
treatments.attending_line: Look at that, someone connected sore throat to shoulder pain. Gold star.

treatments.name: Amoxicillin for strep throat
treatments.why: Mono is viral, amoxicillin causes a classic rash in EBV, and the spleen keeps bleeding.

if_wrong_cascade.text: Kidneys shutting down from low flow

treatments.attending_line: Great, you treated a virus with penicillin while he bleeds out. Bold.

treatments.name: Shoulder sling and more NSAIDs
treatments.why: Shoulder pain is referred from blood irritating the diaphragm, and NSAIDs impair platelets so the bleeding gets worse.
treatments.attending_line: The shoulder's fine. The blood filling his belly isn't.

treatments.name: Adrenaline for anaphylaxis
treatments.why: He's in shock from blood loss, not allergy; adrenaline squeezes vessels without replacing volume and strains the heart.
treatments.attending_line: Wrong kind of shock. He's not allergic, he's empty.

post_mortem: Jonah's spleen was swollen and fragile from mono, and a rugby tackle tore it open, so he bled slowly into his belly until he went into shock. A good doctor would have linked the lingering sore throat and the hit to the body with left shoulder-tip pain (Kehr's sign) and checked for bleeding in the abdomen.
